name: iOS Simulator
description: Private iOS simulators: each task sees its own device in its sidebar tab, and the Simulators view manages them all. Persistent run switch; 15-minute idle shutdown keeps data. Requires macOS 15+, Apple Silicon, full Xcode and an iOS runtime. Built on open-source Baguette (tddworks, Apache-2.0).
whenToUse: Default for iOS Simulator work: install, launch and drive built apps on private devices; screenshot, wait, capture changes, read logs; live view in the task sidebar. Run environment and devices first. Verify with real touches (tap/gesture), not AXe/idb or Xcode windows. heal needs consent.

environment.description: Call first. Checks macOS 15.0+ and Apple Silicon, then reads the bundled Baguette, Xcode, installed iOS runtimes and device types. Downloads nothing.

devices.description: List this plugin's private devices and states, each with tasks (how many tasks use it) and thisTask (assigned to the current task). Reuse this task's device or a free one (tasks 0); never control Cindy embedded or Xcode default devices.

device.description: Manage private devices. create: new device from environment's runtime and deviceType (about 7–12 GB each); only when the task needs a clean device, another model or isolation. boot: start and wait for initialization (about 105 s; on timeout inspect state). shutdown: stop, keeping data. rename: keeps data. erase: wipe all apps and data. delete: remove the device permanently. Use erase and delete only when the user asks. Subject to the run switch; devices stop after 15 idle minutes by default (not while a view is open or a tool is operating them).

app.description: App lifecycle. install: install a locally built simulator .app (absolute appPath; build it with the project's own Xcode workflow). Skips when identical to the installed app, syncs only changed files when few changed, and returns a job for long installs (wait with install_status). info: installed version, build and executable fingerprint; with appPath, matchesLocal says whether this build is the one installed. launch: start it (relaunches by default; arguments, env) and open the live view in this task's sidebar; check viewer.previewOpened (view capabilities: see viewer). terminate; uninstall (deletes its data); open_url (deep link; if iOS asks to open another app, screenshot and tap the prompt).

screenshot.description: Capture the current screen: the image is attached to the result for you to see (older Cindy returns only path; open it with your image tool). Upright as the user sees it, with the screen's corners and Dynamic Island; by default 1 pixel = 1 view point, so coordinates read off the image go straight to tap and gesture. grid=true overlays a labelled grid; region crops a rectangle (small text, borders, safe areas); scale 2–3 for detail (divide coordinates by scale).

describe_ui.description: Read the on-screen elements (accessibility tree). Default: a compact list in reading order with role, text, id, frame and center in view points (tap the center directly). Filter with query/role; x,y returns what is under a point; mode=full returns the whole tree. An empty list usually means a game or custom-drawn UI: use screenshot with grid and coordinates.

tap.description: Real touch tap through the simulator's system touch path: no window, works while the Mac is locked, and the app receives a finger touch. Target an element by text or id (optional role, nth) or a view point x,y. count=2 double-taps; duration≥0.5 long-presses. Returns the new on-screen elements about 0.6 s later by default (observe=ui). Verify interactions with this; do not inject events into the app process, which bypasses the real touch chain.

gesture.description: Swipes and multi-finger gestures, also real touches. kind: swipe (from→to, or direction up/down/left/right; up = finger moves up, content advances); drag (hold for hold seconds, then move to to: drag and drop, reordering); pinch (center, from_spread→to_spread); pan (two fingers by [dx,dy]); edge (system edges: bottom = Home/app switcher, top = Notification or Control Center); scroll_to (swipe until the text or id element is fully visible, or report the end). View points; observe as in tap.

type_text.description: Type into the focused field. text accepts any Unicode, including Chinese (pasted through the simulator clipboard, replacing it); keys sends keys such as Enter, Backspace, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown or cmd+A; clear=true empties the field first. Check focus first and observe the result; key acknowledgements are not app completion.

press.description: Hardware buttons: home, lock, power, volume-up, volume-down, action, app-switcher, swipe-to-app-switcher, swipe-to-home, pull-down-to-notification-center, pull-down-to-lock-screen; duration holds it. release-input only releases stuck keys and stops repeats; it restarts nothing and closes no app.

wait_for.description: Return once a condition holds (up to 90 s) instead of fixed sleeps and repeated screenshots. text or id appears (gone=true: disappears); stable=seconds: the screen stops changing for that long (loading, animations); log=regex: a matching line appears in the app's log (with bundleId). screenshot=true attaches the screen at that moment. A timeout reports what was on screen.

capture.description: Capture a change: start recording frames, run action (tool tap, gesture, press, type_text, open_url or app_launch with its args), keep going for seconds (≤15), drop duplicate frames and return one contact sheet in time order labelled in milliseconds, plus the frame files. For transitions, animations, brief toasts, loading and skeleton screens. Without action it records whatever changes. The contact sheet is attached to the result too.

set_state.description: Change device state, several at once: orientation; posture for foldables (closed/open/flat or degrees); appearance light/dark; contrast; text_size (Dynamic Type); network (profile name, offline, clear or {latency, bandwidth, loss}; applies to apps launched afterwards); location {lat, lon} or clear; status_bar clean (9:41, full bars and battery, for screenshots) or clear; privacy {action grant/revoke/reset, service, bundleId} to pre-answer permission prompts. Returns the new screen size and orientation after orientation or posture changes. Changing a permission terminates that app; set it before launch.

logs.description: Read an app's recent log and crash reports. bundleId or process selects it; last_seconds defaults to 120; level error (errors and faults only), default, info or debug; match filters by regex. Includes this device's recent crash summaries for that process by default (exception, reason, crashed-thread frames).

heal.description: Explicit Baguette repair for iOS 27 input shadowed by Device Hub, using simctl on the private device set. Restarts SpringBoard and terminates running apps; call only after the user accepts that. Try press(release-input) first for stuck keys.

viewer.description: Open (open) or close (close) the device's live view in this task's sidebar. open returns previewOpened; confirm it before saying it is shown. close only stops the view; the device and app keep running. The page is user-operated: input, rotation, shake, screenshots (Desktop or clipboard), device switching and start/stop (stopping ends apps), and Baguette advanced tools: location and motion simulation, status bar and persistent network conditions, camera input, accessibility tree, logs and recording export (may contain app private data); map search and tiles go through the plugin's proxy to OpenStreetMap. Tell the user about these before opening; opening runs none of them. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
